study_identification.author_journal_year: Tong et al., Journal of Affective Disorders, 2024
study_identification.title: Individual deviations from normative electroencephalographic connectivity predict antidepressant response

study_characteristics.study_objective: To develop a normative modeling framework based on resting-state EEG functional connectivity to identify clinically translatable pretreatment biomarkers for antidepressant response prediction in MDD patients. The study aimed to quantify individual deviations in psychopathological dimensions and enable individual-level prediction of sertraline and placebo treatment responses.

hc_n.answer: 154 (8 from EMBARC, 75 from Depression-EEG, 71 from LEMON)

hc_age.answer: EMBARC: mean 21.6, sd 2.8; Depression-EEG: mean 19.0, sd 1.2; LEMON: mean 22.5 (age 18-25 for all cohorts used for normative modeling)

preprocessing_pipeline.answer: Brainstorm toolbox; Minimum-norm estimation for source localization; OpenMEEG plugin (FreeSurfer average brain template); Power envelope connectivity (PEC) calculation; Hilbert transform; Schaefer atlas with 100 brain regions; Automated artifact rejection pipeline; Independent component analysis; Frequency bands: theta (4-7 Hz), alpha (8-12 Hz), beta (13-30 Hz), low gamma (31-50 Hz); ComBat harmonization

quality_checking_detail.answer: Fully automated artifact rejection pipeline including: (1) resampling to 250 Hz, (2) removal of 60 Hz line noise, (3) 0.01 Hz high-pass filter, (4) rejection of bad epochs by magnitude thresholding, (5) rejection of bad channels by spatial correlation thresholding, (6) exclusion of subjects with >20% bad channels, (7) spherical spline interpolation for bad channels, (8) independent component analysis to remove artifacts (scalp muscle, ocular, ECG), (9) re-referencing to common average. For MDD patients: 21 patients excluded for missing baseline EEG data, 13 excluded for low data quality.

site_effect_handling_detail.answer: ComBat harmonization using empirical Bayesian methods across three independent cohorts (Depression-EEG, EMBARC, LEMON). Batch labels assigned based on cohort origin. Age incorporated as covariate in data harmonization to ensure eliminated differences were site effects. Transformation matrices trained on healthy controls then applied to MDD patients to prevent data leakage. Each EEG condition (four frequency bands in either eyes-open or eyes-closed paradigms, totally eight conditions) was processed individually. Comparison with unharmonized data showed inferior prediction performance without harmonization (Supplementary Tables 2, 3).

response_variable.answer: Power envelope connectivity (PEC) across 4950 functional connections (100 ROI pairs from Schaefer atlas); Separate models for eight EEG conditions: theta, alpha, beta, gamma frequency bands in eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions

predictor_variables.answer: No explicit predictors (unsupervised autoencoder-based approach); Age was used as covariate in ComBat harmonization

predictor_effects.answer: Unsupervised normative modeling without pre-defined covariates. Age was included as covariate in ComBat harmonization (not in the autoencoder itself). The autoencoder learns representative dimensions of healthy controls without supervision.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study appropriately handles nuisance structure in multiple ways. First, ComBat harmonization with age as covariate addresses mean shifts and variance differences across three independent cohorts. Second, the autoencoder with L2-norm constraint reduces collinearity between functional connections. Third, normalization strategy (inverse hyperbolic tangent transformation followed by z-scoring) was conducted on each subject independently to ensure independence from other subjects. Fourth, age calibration was performed by regressing out age from individual deviation features to ensure brain signatures were not confounded by age. The study explicitly verified that prediction residuals were independent of age and that individual deviation dimensions were orthogonal to age dimension.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: ComBat harmonization: 'The utilization of multiple independent cohorts requires data harmonization to eliminate potential site effects due to different data acquisition protocols across studies. The data harmonization was realized with a MATLAB package built on empirical Bayesian methods (ComBat), which applied a unique transformation on the data from each independent cohorts to project them to a common space... we incorporated age as a covariate in the data harmonization to ensure the eliminated differences were indeed site effects.' Age calibration: 'as individual deviations in many EEG conditions could predict age (Supplementary Table 6), and age showed modest correlation with placebo response (Supplementary Fig. 2), we regressed out age from individual deviation features to ensure that the brain signatures we identified were not confounded by age.' Verification: 'Correlation analyses revealed no correlation between sertraline response and age (r=0.04, p=0.67, Supplementary Fig. 2a), and absolute prediction residuals were also independent of age (EO-alpha: r=-0.09, p=0.36; EO-gamma: r=-0.09, p=0.37, Supplementary Fig. 2c, d). A further analysis confirmed that the individual deviation dimensions of sertraline response and age were orthogonal (Inner products of age dimension and sertraline response dimension: EO-alpha: -0.007; EO-gamma: -0.028).'
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.location: Supplementary Methods, Data Harmonization section; Main text page regarding age calibration in Section 2.7 Treatment response prediction; Main text Section 2.6 regarding autoencoder training

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The study validated the normative model using cross-validation within the same healthy control dataset. For comparing individual deviations between healthy controls and MDD patients, the authors explicitly state they used cross-validation for healthy controls to ensure fair comparison, rather than using subjects from the training set.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.supporting_text: 'we tested whether indeed the reconstructed rsEEG FC captured the variability in healthy controls and the reconstruction error reflected deviations in psychopathological dimensions. To this end, we first compared the distributions of individual deviations for healthy controls and patient groups. To ensure a fair comparison, we evaluated the individual deviations of healthy controls with cross-validation instead of the subjects used for normative modeling training. Encouragingly, the results revealed that MDD patients were associated with significantly greater individual deviations than healthy controls for all EEG conditions (Supplementary Fig. 6), confirming that the normative model captured general variability in healthy controls.' Supplementary Figure 6 caption: 'To ensure a fair comparison, cross-validation is conducted for HC subjects to evaluate the individual deviations on test data.'
nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.location: Main text Section 3.4 Normative modeling distinguishes subclinical and diagnostic variabilities; Supplementary Figure 6 caption

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The study does not validate the normative model using an independent healthy control dataset from the same domain. All healthy controls from the three cohorts (EMBARC, Depression-EEG, LEMON) were used for training the normative model after harmonization. While cross-validation was performed within this combined dataset, no truly independent healthy control cohort was held out or used for external validation.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: The methods describe: 'we developed healthy norms of 154 young adults (age 18-25), which consist of 8 subjects from the EMBARC cohort, 75 subjects from the depression-EEG cohort, and 71 subjects from the LEMON cohort.' All three cohorts were combined and used for training: 'Above all, the normalized EEG FC data of healthy controls from the three cohorts (Depression-EEG, EMBARC, LEMON) were combined and used as the input data matrix.' No mention of external independent healthy control validation cohort.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.location: Main text Section 2.3 Normative modeling of functional connectivity; Supplementary Methods Data Harmonization section

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study demonstrates some level of different domain validation through leave-study-site-out analysis for the predictive models. The normative model was trained on healthy young adults (age 18-25) but successfully applied to predict treatment responses in older MDD patients (mean age ~38 years), and the study verified that predictions were age-independent. However, this is not a full external validation on a completely independent dataset from a different domain, but rather demonstrates generalizability across age ranges and study sites within the same overall study framework (EMBARC). The study acknowledges that replication with additional independent cohorts is needed.
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.supporting_text: Leave-study-site-out analysis: 'Leave-study-site-out analysis further confirmed that the sertraline response prediction model exhibited significant predictability for data from held-out study sites (r=0.30, p=0.0022, Supplementary Fig. 4a), demonstrating its potential generalizability to independent cohorts.' Age generalization: 'As the individual deviations used for sertraline and placebo response prediction were derived from a healthy norm of young adults, we examined whether the prediction performance was dependent on age... A further analysis confirmed that the individual deviation dimensions of sertraline response and age were orthogonal... justifying that the normative modeling based on healthy young adults was capable of predicting sertraline responses of elder MDD patients.' Limitation acknowledged: 'Although our results were preliminarily verified with aforementioned analyses, replication studies with additional independent cohorts are important to confirm our findings of rsEEG connectivity-based individual deviations and predictive modeling for sertraline and placebo responses.'
nm_vldtn_diff_domain.location: Main text Section 3.1, Section 2.6; Supplementary Figure 4; Discussion section

clinical_dataset.answer: EMBARC (Establishing Moderators and Biosignatures of Antidepressant Response for Clinical Care)

clinical_groups_age.answer: Sertraline: mean 38.6, sd 14.1; Placebo: mean 37.5, sd 13.0; Overall age range 18-65

deviation_metric.answer: Reconstruction error (autoencoder-based individual deviation): difference between original EEG FC and reconstructed EEG FC. Individual deviations quantified for 4950 functional connections across eight EEG conditions (four frequency bands × two eye conditions).

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: Connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) to select features significantly correlated with HAMD17 score change (threshold p<0.05); Age regression to remove age confounds; LASSO regression with inner-loop 10-fold cross-validation for sparsity parameter selection; 10-fold cross-validation repeated 10 times with median predicted outcomes; Performance quantified as Pearson's correlation coefficient and R-squared between actual and predicted outcomes; Leave-study-site-out analysis for generalizability assessment; Comparison of feature importance across treatment arms using Wilcoxon's rank-sum tests; Fisher's z-test to compare prediction performance across models.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Individual deviations from normative EEG connectivity significantly predicted sertraline response (EO-gamma: r=0.43, p<0.001, R²=0.15) and placebo response (EC-beta: r=0.33, p<0.001), with treatment-specific signatures suggesting distinct neural pathways for sertraline (transmodal networks) versus placebo (non-transmodal networks) responses.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The autoencoder-based normative modeling framework successfully predicted treatment responses with high specificity to treatment arms. For sertraline (n=102), connectivity deviations in eyes-open-gamma condition yielded best prediction (r=0.43, R²=0.15, pFDR=4.74×10⁻⁵), significantly outperforming raw EEG FC features (r=0.17, p=0.021), PCA-based (r=0.15, p=0.015), and regression-based (r=0.20, p=0.032) individual deviations. EO-alpha also showed significant prediction (r=0.33, pFDR=0.0076). For placebo (n=119), EC-beta condition was most predictive (r=0.33, pFDR=0.0019), outperforming raw FC (r=-0.03, p=0.002), PCA-based (r=0.15, p=0.076), and regression-based (r=0.07, p=0.019) approaches. EC-theta also predicted placebo response (r=0.26, pFDR=0.015). Importantly, models showed treatment specificity: sertraline model did not predict placebo (r=0.03, p=0.74) and vice versa (r=0.10, p=0.32). Leave-study-site-out analysis confirmed generalizability (sertraline: r=0.30, p=0.0022; placebo: r=0.22, p=0.0155). Network-level analysis revealed distinct pathways: non-transmodal FCs (visual and somatomotor networks) showed significantly higher importance for placebo response (p=0.009), while transmodal FCs (default mode and frontoparietal networks) showed higher importance for sertraline versus placebo (p=0.035). The normative model successfully distinguished subclinical and diagnostic variabilities: MDD patients showed significantly greater individual deviations than healthy controls across all conditions; diagnostic measures showed stronger correlation with individual deviations while subclinical measures correlated more with reconstructed FCs. The EEG-based models outperformed clinical measure-based predictions (134 item-level scores: sertraline r=0.22, placebo r=0.03).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: The study acknowledges several limitations. First, replication studies with additional independent cohorts are needed to confirm the findings. Second, the EMBARC protocol did not collect neuroimaging data at the end of treatment, preventing confirmation of brain connectivity alterations mediated by medications. Third, future work with larger sample size is warranted to explore potential overlapping between healthy controls and patients. Fourth, validation of the framework's generalizability to other antidepressants, psychotherapy, neurostimulation therapy, and other psychiatric disorders is needed. Fifth, the normative model was based on young adults (age 18-25), though the study demonstrated age-independence of predictions for older MDD patients.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The study demonstrates a highly generalizable framework combining autoencoder-based normative modeling with connectome-based predictive modeling. Key innovations include: (1) unsupervised learning without dependence on pre-selected covariates, (2) processing all ROI-ROI connectivity together as single entity to account for interactions, (3) distance-based mapping of individual deviations without dependence on prediction models, (4) successful harmonization across three independent cohorts with different acquisition protocols, (5) treatment-specific biomarkers suggesting distinct neurobiological pathways. The framework is clinically translatable as EEG is cost-effective and user-friendly compared to fMRI. Most important connections for sertraline (EO-gamma): precuneus-superior occipital gyrus, postcentral gyrus-inferior temporal gyrus, precuneus-angular gyrus. For placebo (EC-beta): middle frontal gyrus-calcarine sulcus, orbitofrontal cortex-calcarine sulcus, superior temporal gyrus-precuneus. The study provides neurobiological insights suggesting sertraline achieves effects through higher-level transmodal networks while placebo operates through more superficial non-transmodal pathways, aligning with findings that placebo tends to have earlier onset but is more prone to relapse.

general_notes.general_notes: This is an EEG-based normative modeling study, which is relatively rare in the normative modeling literature that predominantly uses structural and functional MRI. The study represents one of the first applications of functional connectivity-based normative modeling using EEG data for psychiatric treatment prediction. NCT registration: NCT01407094. The EMBARC study included four sites: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center, Massachusetts General Hospital, Columbia University, and University of Michigan. EEG was recorded with different systems across sites (BioSemi 72-channel, Geodesic Net 129-channel, NeuroScan Synamp 60-channel, NeuroScan Synamp 62-channel), with 54 common channels used for analysis. The study compared three normative modeling approaches: PCA-based, regression-based (Rutherford et al., 2022 framework), and autoencoder-based, with autoencoder showing superior performance. The study used power envelope connectivity (PEC) to mitigate spurious correlations from volume conduction. Source localization used minimum-norm estimation with 3003 vertices projected to 100 ROIs (Schaefer atlas). The autoencoder architecture: input layer 4950 (number of FCs), hidden layer 500 (reduced dimensionality), output layer 4950; sigmoid activation; L2-norm constraint. Treatment specificity was rigorously demonstrated: predicted sertraline and placebo responses showed no correlation (r=0.05, p=0.46) and were orthogonal (inner product=-5.23×10⁻⁴). Sertraline dosing: started at 50mg, increased to maximum 200mg if tolerated and needed. Treatment duration: 8 weeks. Outcome measure: change in HAMD-17 score (pre-treatment minus post-treatment). The study explicitly verified age-independence: sertraline response not correlated with age (r=0.04, p=0.67), prediction residuals independent of age, and individual deviation dimensions orthogonal to age dimension (inner products: EO-alpha -0.007, EO-gamma -0.028).
